subject: Acme Analytics: remediation offer & roll‑forward compensation plan
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Latency spikes last week — request for remediation & credit

Hi Olga,

We had a pretty disruptive window last Thursday (04/09) where a burst of requests to the text-generation endpoint caused sustained tail latency (~3–8s) across a subset of our jobs. That translated to 14 failed pipeline runs and several SLA misses for our end customers. I've attached a short CSV with sampled request logs and a one‑page timeline.

We appreciate the outreach from support but we need a concrete remediation plan and a proposal for compensation for business impact — ideally a combination of credits and a short-term operational support package while we stabilize. Please let me know what you can offer and if you need anything else from our side.

Thanks,
Sarah Lee
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics
[sample attachments: acme-latency-sample-logs.csv (csv), incident-timeline-20260409.pdf (pdf)]
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spikes last week — request for remediation & credit

Hi Sarah — thanks for the logs and timeline. I'm really sorry this happened. We've reviewed your samples and correlated them with a transient autoscaling/queueing interaction in our EU-west routing pool that spilled over into your US region path for a short window.

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Hotfix deployed to routing policy to eliminate the fallback loop that amplified tail latency.
- Enabled prefix KV caching for your model variant to reduce repeated load during bursts.
- Jonas' team will run a 48‑hour enhanced monitoring watch and share daily health updates.

For compensation, our standard make‑good is a one‑month service credit for incidents that meet threshold. Given the impact you describe and Acme's strategic usage, Karthik and I are preparing a bespoke proposal: 2–3 months of credit + a one‑time account credit to offset failed job costs + 30 days of prioritized engineering support to stabilize throughput.

I'll loop in Karthik and request executive approval for anything beyond our standard one‑month policy. Expect an internal follow‑up today.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme Analytics outage impact — ask for exec concession approval

Marissa — forwarding the thread and initial findings from Olga/Jonas. Acme is a mid‑enterprise account with strong expansion potential in Q3; they run high‑value pipelines that exposed us to visible customer impact (14 failed runs, internal remediation costs for their team).

Attached is a simple model that maps revenue at risk, estimated cost to the customer of failed runs, and proposed concession buckets. Quick summary:
- Standard policy: 1 month service credit.
- Proposed (recommended by sales): 3 months service credit applied to next invoice + one‑time $15,000 account credit to reimburse their failed batch costs + 30 days of prioritized SRE support (no charge).

Rationale: preserves the relationship, reduces churn risk, and buys runway for our teams to jointly tune their workload. Requesting your sign‑off for a one‑off exception to policy for up to $15k plus time‑bound credits. If you prefer a smaller credit, suggested alternate is 2 months + $8k.

Attachments: makegood-model.xlsx

Can you confirm approval or suggest limits? We need to keep precedent low and mark this as an executive exception if approved. If approved, I'll ask Legal to draft an amendment and Finance to validate the accounting treatment.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme Analytics outage impact — ask for exec concession approval

Karthik / team — thanks for the diligence and the clear model. I understand the strategic considerations. Approve the following one‑time concession with the expectation we document precedent and limit similar exceptions:
- 3 months of service credit (applied to next two invoices as 50%/50%)
- $12,000 one‑time account credit (cap) to reimburse failed job impact
- 30 days prioritized SRE support (no charge)

Conditions:
1) Legal drafts an amendment that explicitly states this is a one‑off executive concession, non‑precedential.
2) Finance confirms write‑off accounting and sets the credit code.
3) Sales documents the remediation plan and a post‑mortem to be shared with Acme within 10 business days.

Please proceed; keep me on thread for final doc.

-Marissa
VP, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Legal <legal@redwood.com>, Finance <billing@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency spikes last week — remediation & compensation proposal

Hi Sarah — thanks again for your patience while we reviewed this. Per our conversation and internal approval, here's the formal offer:

Offer summary (one‑time, executive concession):
- 3 months of service credit (applied as two credits across next two invoices)
- $12,000 one‑time account credit to offset failed runs
- 30 days of prioritized SRE support to help tune throughput and apply best‑practice configs

Next steps:
1) Our Legal team will send a short amendment for signature through DocuSign (link below). Please have your legal review and countersign.
2) Finance will apply the credits after we receive a fully executed amendment.
3) Jonas will initiate the 48‑hour watch tomorrow and follow with a 10‑day post‑mortem and tuning plan.

DocuSign (draft): https://docusign.example.com/ENVELOPE-ACME-2026-0418
Attachments: proposed-amendment-docusign.pdf

If that is acceptable, please reply with approval and we'll get the DocuSign sent to your legal. We're committed to keeping Acme stable and preventing recurrence.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
